question.title: Identifying Consecutive Logins
question.desc: Find the user IDs of users who have logged in for three consecutive days. The login table contains user IDs and login dates.
question.setup: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS login; CREATE TABLE login (user_id INTEGER, login_date DATE); INSERT INTO login (user_id, login_date) VALUES (1, '2022-01-01'), (1, '2022-01-02'), (1, '2022-01-03'), (2, '2022-01-02'), (2, '2022-01-03'), (2, '2022-01-04');
question.solution: WITH ranked_logins AS ( SELECT user_id, login_date, DATE_TRUNC('day', login_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS consecutive_group FROM login ) SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM ranked_logins GROUP BY user_id, consecutive_group HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;
question.tips: Consider using window functions for efficiently handling sequences.
hints: You might need to use a window function to track the sequence of logins.
The DATE_TRUNC function could help in comparing dates by removing the time component, and ROW_NUMBER can help in assigning a unique number to each row within a partition of a result set.
Use a Common Table Expression (CTE) to first identify sequences and then filter based on the length of these sequences.
